sections.html:
Monroe County's seat, Bloomington, is in south-central Indiana, and no single thing moves its housing market like Indiana University. About 83,307 people lived in the city as of July 2025, which ranks it seventh in the state, and the median age in 2020 was 25.1. Students, staff and renters make up much of the population. A family home on the west or south side attracts a different buyer from a duplex near campus.

Housing measureBloomington, 2020 to 2024
Owner-occupied housing unit rate34.7%
Median value of owner-occupied units$321,400
Households34,514
Persons per household1.91
Median gross rent$1,200

With roughly a third of homes owner-occupied, rentals make up a big part of the stock. Owners of those rentals face the city rules below long before a buyer shows up.

The city stands on high ground between the West and East Forks of the White River. It was founded by settlers in 1818 and incorporated in 1827. Indiana University was established in 1820, and its Bloomington campus now enrolls more than 45,000 students. The campus and downtown Courthouse Square sit close together, and the older neighborhoods around them include several historic districts:

  • Courthouse Square Historic District
  • Prospect Hill and Vinegar Hill
  • North Washington Street and Bloomington West Side
  • Steele Dunning and University Courts

Houses in these districts tend to have aging wiring, plumbing and foundations, and loan-dependent buyers often balk. Cash buyers accept the house as it is, so the repair haggling that stalls so many older-home sales never starts.

Karst limestone underlies Bloomington, and sinkholes, caves and underground streams come with it. Clear Creek is the biggest stream in town.

Walk the lot, not just the rooms. A dip in the yard, a drain that will not empty or a cracked foundation invites questions at inspection. No diagnosis is required before you sell, but hiding what you know is a mistake. Selling as-is for cash means you can state the condition plainly and skip paying for repairs first.

Roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take a beating from humid summers and cold winters.

City rules require every rental inside the limits to be registered with, and inspected by, Housing and Neighborhood Development, called HAND. Indiana University's own property is exempt. Penalties for an unregistered rental run up to $100 per day.

These are the steps and costs to know if you are selling a house with tenants:

  • The first inspection is usually scheduled within 2 business days of registration.
  • The inspection report comes 2 to 3 weeks later.
  • Repairs are due within 60 days, with select exterior repairs allowed one year.
  • Reinspections beyond the included one cost $77, and a missed appointment costs $50.
  • Permits are issued for 3, 4 or 5 years.
  • A 25% permit fee discount applies if no violations are found at the first inspection.

In single-family zones the usual limit is one family or three unrelated adults, though some properties are grandfathered. Have HAND confirm legal occupancy before you advertise a house as a rental or sell to someone who intends to rent it. Also ask whether the permit passes to a new owner.

You can read the rules on the City of Bloomington rental occupancy page.

sections.h2: Monroe County property taxes at closing
sections.html:
Taxes come due in two installments, normally May 10 and November 10, moved to the next business day if the date falls on a weekend or holiday. Bills go to the owner of record as of January 1.

A payment inside 30 days of the due date, with no back taxes owed, draws a 5 percent penalty. After that the penalty is 10 percent.

At a Bloomington closing the title company usually prorates the tax between buyer and seller. To check a balance before you sell, call the Treasurer at (812) 349-7333 or write to treasurer@co.monroe.in.us. The office is at the Monroe County Courthouse, 100 W Kirkwood Ave. A bill stamped "IN ESCROW" means your lender asked for a copy and may already be paying it.

The Monroe County Treasurer posts the current schedule.

An occupied rental can be sold, but the paperwork has to line up. Read the lease for its end date and its notice terms, then tell any buyer who lives there and what rent is paid. Confirm with HAND that the property is registered and whether an inspection is due, since an overdue inspection is something a buyer will want settled or priced in.

If the tenants will leave before closing, plan for the unit to be worn after a move-out. A cash buyer takes the house in that state, which saves you the cleaning, repainting and re-listing that a conventional sale would expect.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Bloomington
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so there is no appraisal contingency and no loan underwriting to wait on. You send the address and condition, we review it, and if you want the offer you pick a closing date at a local title company.

The calendar of a university town matters. Move-outs peak when the school year ends, and turnover can leave a landlord with a vacant, worn unit. Landlords who would rather not repaint, re-carpet and re-list a tired property are a common reason a cash offer makes sense here.

Interstate 69 reached Bloomington in December 2015, State Road 37 now ends at an I-69 interchange on the south side, and State Roads 45 and 46 share a four-lane bypass. Indianapolis International Airport is about 50 miles away, which helps owners who live out of state and want to handle the sale by phone.

  • Inherited homes in older neighborhoods
  • Rentals that failed or are overdue for a HAND inspection
  • Houses with deferred repairs the owner cannot afford
  • Landlords leaving the business

Closing day is simple on your side. You sign at the title company, the title company pays off any mortgage and open tax from the proceeds, and the deed is recorded. Out-of-town owners can usually handle the signing by mail or remote signing.

Before you accept an offer, ask for the closing timeline in writing, find out who pays each closing fee, and tell the title company about any tenant and any open HAND inspection so the paperwork matches the house.

faqs.q: Do I need a HAND permit to sell a rental house in Bloomington?
faqs.a: Registration applies to rentals while they are rented, not to the act of selling. An active rental needs to be registered, and an unregistered one can be penalized up to $100 per day. Ask HAND whether the existing permit stays with the property after a sale.

faqs.q: Is Bloomington a good place to sell an older house as-is?
faqs.a: Often yes, because many homes sit in older historic districts where repairs get expensive. A cash buyer can take the house in its current condition, so you skip inspection repair requests. The offer price reflects the work needed.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Bloomington, Indiana?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied housing units is $321,400 for 2020 to 2024. Individual houses vary widely, and a cash offer depends on the condition of your specific property.

faqs.q: When is the next Monroe County property tax due date?
faqs.a: Installments are normally due May 10 and November 10, shifted to the next business day when needed. Check the Treasurer's page for the current schedule.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bloomington house with tenants still living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. We can buy an occupied rental, though lease terms and notice rules matter, so tell us about the tenants when you reach out. Registration status with HAND is also worth confirming before closing.
